rv.q: "The director Michael Wilson has assembled a very worthy revival of Arthur Miller’s very worthy 1964 play, 'Incident at Vichy' which is a pleasure and a problem….Incident at Vichy is an occasionally poignant play...The pessimistic philosophy is somehow too assured.

"Directed somberly by Michael Wilson, 'Incident at Vichy' depicts 10 men who have been rounded up by the police on suspicion of being Jewish; their papers and their anatomy are to be checked...Earnest urgency often sounds like an essay or a lecture...The paradox of this highly discursive work is that the characters who say the least are in some...
